newsitem.title: UK: Cook on trip to seal Britain's new start in Europe.
newsitem.headline: Cook on trip to seal Britain's new start in Europe.

text.p: British Foreign Secretary Robin Cook embarked on his first trip abroad on Wednesday, heading for France and Germany to seal the new Labour government's pledge to make a new start with Europe.
European Union matters and the NATO alliance are high on the agenda of Cook's talks with his counterparts in Paris and Bonn, British officials said.
Cook, installed last week after the Labour Party swept back to power after 18 years, will also meet opposition leaders in both countries.
"His visit reflects the government's determination to make a fresh start on a new and constructive relationship with Europe," a Foreign Office official said.
The Labour government has pledged to scrap the increasingly antagonistic tone towards Europe taken by the outgoing Conservative administration.

It has said it will sign the Social Chapter of the Maastricht Treaty at the EU's Amsterdam summit in June and says ministers rather than civil servants will attend all future talks on European integration.

Britain has said it is unlikely that it will join the European single currency in the first wave. But it has said it will agree to more qualified majority voting in some policy areas and support a new employment chapter in a new EU treaty.
In Paris, Cook will go first to meet Socialist Party leader Lionel Jospin and will then meet French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette over lunch.
He will then travel to Bonn for talks with German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.
